title: Nasdaq-100 Futures Sink 2% After Big Tech Earnings, Treasuries Rally
summary: Gotrade News - Nasdaq 100 futures fell 2% on Thursday evening, October 29, after reports from Amazon (AMZN) and Intel (INTC) disappointed investors,
body_markdown:
For the fourth quarter, Amazon expects net sales of $240.0 billion to $247.0 billion, growth of 12% to 16% from a year earlier, and operating income of $28.5 billion to $33.5 billion, compared with $25.0 billion in the fourth quarter of 2025, according to the company.


## Intel Guides Q4 Revenue to $15 Billion to $16 Billion


Intel's third-quarter revenue rose 21% to $16.5 billion, according to the company's release, with Data Center and AI revenue up 78% to $7.3 billion and Intel Foundry up 58% to $6.7 billion, while the Client Computing and Physical AI Group fell 5% to $8.1 billion.


Investing.com said the strong third-quarter profit was vastly outweighed by disappointing forecasts for the fourth quarter. Intel guided fourth-quarter revenue to $15.0 billion to $16.0 billion and non-GAAP EPS to $0.25, with non-GAAP gross margin of 38.0%, down from 44.1% in the third quarter. On the earnings call, analyst Ben Reitzes said the revenue guide was "about $1.8 billion below the street," as reported by Investing.com.


CEO Lip-Bu Tan cited "industry-wide impacts from higher memory prices and limited IT budgets," and what he called an "unfortunate and tragic accident" that led to an extended shutdown at Intel's Israel factory. CFO Dave Zinsner estimated that the shutdown would cut fourth-quarter revenue by about $300 million and weigh on gross margin by roughly 200 basis points.


## Why Are Nasdaq 100 Futures Down?


Nasdaq 100 futures fell as the Amazon and Intel reports landed on top of AI spending worries, according to Investing.com, which noted that underwhelming earnings from memory chip giant Samsung Electronics had added to growing concerns over stretched AI spending. As of 20:47 ET, Nasdaq 100 futures stood at 28,975.0, S&P 500 futures were down 0.8% at 7,690.25, and Dow Jones futures were up 0.04% at 52,533.0.


The evening drop followed a regular session in which the Nasdaq Composite slid 1.4%, pressured by a steep fall in[Alphabet (GOOGL)](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/us-stock/googl/) after its[third-quarter results](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/news/alphabet-q3-earnings-miss-sinks-stock-reignites-ai-capex-fears-googl-nasdaq-futures/) showed a deterioration in margins from AI-related spending, the outlet reported. The Dow fell the least as investors pivoted into defensive sectors such as healthcare and utilities.


Treasuries rallied in that session. According to[Investrade](https://investrade.com/market-review-october-29-2026/) , the 10-year yield fell 5.6 basis points to 4.988%, and the 2-year yield dropped 7.7 basis points to 4.65%, its lowest level in a week, as softer PCE inflation data helped ease pressure. Amazon and Intel reported after a[busy Thursday of economic data](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/news/amazon-intel-gdp-and-pce-tonight/) : third-quarter GDP grew at a 3.4% annualized rate against the 3.1% economists expected, while the third-quarter PCE price index rose 2.1% against a 2.6% consensus and core PCE rose 2.5% against 2.4%, Investrade reported.


Per Investing.com, the Federal Reserve held interest rates at 4.0% earlier in the week, the stronger-than-expected GDP and PCE data furthered bets on a December rate hike, and Fed Chair Kevin Warsh reiterated the central bank's commitment to its 2% inflation target.
